result.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
result.summary: Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance. Drawing on a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, a meta-agent coordinates harness development from historical designs with model checkpoint selection or merging and subsequent adaptation under the selected harness, aligning inherited capabilities with evolving execution requirements to reduce brain--body mismatch. Using only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on its own rejection-sampled trajectories, CoEvo-RSI makes Qwen3.5-9B competitive with larger models across diverse vertical applications, including multi-agent failure attribution, role-aware text-to-SQL, and smart-home instruction following. It surpasses DeepSeek-V4-Pro on TraceElephant (+14.16 agent accuracy) and GLM-5.3 on HomeBench VM (+4.90 success rate), underscoring the need for brain--body alignment and the potential of bidirectional historical inheritance to advance agent co-evolution.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CoEvo-RSI，让 agent 的执行脚手架（harness）与模型检查点基于共享演化档案和执行反馈进行双向共同演化，以缓解「脑—体不匹配」，仅用自采样轨迹的 SFT 在多个垂直任务上提升 9B 模型表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 latent visual reasoning 主线无直接关系，但其检查点选择/合并与拒绝采样轨迹监督的协同机制，可能为 LVR 中轨迹训练、监督信号分配与状态更新的配合提供可供核查的方法线索。
